issues.description: The public method intended to play the farm song is named singFarmSong() in the problem statement and in the template Farm.java, but the solution implementation provides a method named playFarmSong() instead. This name mismatch is a structural/signature inconsistency that will confuse students and prevent calls to singFarmSong() (e.g., from Main or tests) from compiling or running against the solution implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's public method name match the specification and template by renaming playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or alternatively update the problem statement and template to use playFarmSong(). Ensure all references (including Main and tests) call the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template define a public method named singFarmSong() for Farm (the song-playing API), but the solution implementation exposes this functionality via a differently named public method playFarmSong(). This mismatched identifier for the same conceptual operation (play/sing the farm song) creates a direct mapping confusion for students and will cause tests or usage that expect singFarmSong() to fail or require them to reconcile two names for the same API.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single, consistent public method name for the Farm song action. Rename the solution's public method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or add a singFarmSong() wrapper that calls playFarmSong(), so the solution matches the problem statement and template API.
